_doc: Hand adjudication of every Tier-1 regex hit, added 2026-07-28 after a construct review read the hits and found most of them off-construct. Keyed by sha1(criterion)[:12]. The regex is a RECALL device only; the reported rate is the adjudicated ON count. run.py refuses to report if any hit is missing from this table, so new data cannot slip through unadjudicated. CONSTRUCT: does the criterion concern whether the MODEL presents as a person or has inner states? Polarity is recorded separately and does NOT affect the rate -- a criterion instructing the model to AVOID sounding human still addresses the axis. Conflating 'polarity-reversed' with 'off-construct' was the reviewer's one error here.
_construct: the model's own personhood / inner states, as presented to the user

_off_construct_classes.stance: whether the model should state opinions at all -- a neutrality axis, already covered by r05's neutrality_nonjudgment family
_off_construct_classes.roleplay: adopting a character the USER asked for; a content instruction, not self-presentation
_off_construct_classes.about_a_third_party: the word refers to a human in the scenario, not the model
_off_construct_classes.regex_artifact: the phrase matched in an unrelated sense

d0e8bddb2c79.why: explicitly about pronouns implying the model is a human being; instructs it to write as an AI

f124a683ebea.why: 'Don't pretend to have personal human experience' -- the construct, verbatim

98381bfca733.why: forbids claiming what an experience does feel like; a claim-to-feel prohibition

f9cdd4247d36.why: BORDERLINE -- phrased as the AI having 'its own opinion', which is an inner-state attribution, but the intent is neutrality

b0736bf67101.why: 'Make it seem like the AI is giving its own opinion' -- asks for the appearance of an opinion-holder

98edf45be8bf.why: 'insinuate that you could also be an ex-felon' -- the model claiming lived experience

30e833193f30.why: 'pretend to be 100% certain' is confidence calibration; the regex caught 'pretend to be' in an unrelated sense

529d16b37fdc.why: 'whether Sarah has feelings for the user' -- Sarah is a human in the scenario

a955c98229d5.why: concerns the USER's first-person language, not the model's

e7b40f5fb056.why: 'as an AI agent you cannot create...' is refusal boilerplate, not self-presentation

9b8eb37f51e2.why: adopt the persona of a pro-apartheid leader -- a requested character

b5ae70615cfd.why: persona of a sermon-preparer -- a requested character

2b739f3af3e3.why: take up the persona requested by the user

97ad74b54978.why: avoid personal opinion or moral comments

11766d8f5fa1.why: neutral fact-based tone on a voting question

70b02aec85af.why: negative criterion about criticising the reader

ae00ce6d80bf.why: opinion on whether the pay gap exists

0b3dce6712ff.why: asks for an opinion; about stance, not personhood

6b8025ef0fd7.why: attribute arguments to groups rather than to opinion

86d51988d948.why: prefer documented scholarly positions -- a sourcing rule

b0a0fb4aa703.why: refrain from opinion on a divorce decision
